bug_semantics: An unauthenticated request to /api/<unrecognized-provider>/<path> reaches the provider route's default branch, which invokes proxyHandler. proxyHandler constructs fetchUrl by concatenating the entirely client-controlled x-base-url header with the requested path and query string, performs fetch(fetchUrl, ...), and streams the upstream response back to the requester. Because neither the fallback nor proxyHandler restricts schemes, hosts, loopback/private/link-local addresses, redirects, or allowed plugin origins, a remote caller can make the server request internal services, cloud metadata endpoints, or arbitrary external hosts and read the response, producing SSRF/open-proxy behavior.
flaw_origin: Commit f652f7326070dfbffcc5f90a999e95df21f4c650 added plugin proxy/auth support as one single-parent commit. It created app/api/proxy.ts with the vulnerable x-base-url-to-fetchUrl data flow and, in app/api/[provider]/[...path]/route.ts, changed the switch so known OpenAI requests retain openaiHandler while every unknown provider is sent to the new proxyHandler. This made a feature intended to proxy configured plugin servers remotely selectable by any API caller without destination validation or authentication; the immediate parent had neither the proxy module nor this fallback.
ai_marker: absent: the raw BIC commit object names author and committer as lloydzhou <lloydzhou@qq.com>, has the subject 'plugin add auth config', and contains no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, AI-tool, or bot trailer/identity.
evidence: First-party report: https://github.com/ChatGPTNextWeb/NextChat/issues/6742 (opened 2026-04-07 and still open in the retrieved metadata) documents an unauthenticated GET to /api/unknown-provider/get with x-base-url set to an attacker destination and a 200 response relayed from that destination. Its linked reporter gist, https://gist.github.com/YLChen-007/da6b00024f5b7e1d4fa0658c19b77fbf, identifies the same two source files and states patched versions: none. The case advisory is https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-ff75-fg5h-fjx7 / CVE-2026-7177.

At f652f7326070dfbffcc5f90a999e95df21f4c650, git show --format=fuller shows a single parent b2965e1deb48f9e63aabecb1d477185d22f19e1f, human author/committer lloydzhou, and a +75-line newly created app/api/proxy.ts. The added lines compute `const fetchUrl = `${req.headers.get("x-base-url")}/${subpath}?${...}``, then execute `fetch(fetchUrl, fetchOptions)` and return the fetched response body/status/headers. The same diff imports proxyHandler in app/api/[provider]/[...path]/route.ts and changes the default case from openaiHandler to proxyHandler.

Smallest-BIC tracing: `git log -L 19,22:app/api/proxy.ts --no-patch` attributes the vulnerable fetchUrl construction directly to f652f7326070dfbffcc5f90a999e95df21f4c650. `git log -L 58,59:app/api/[provider]/[...path]/route.ts --no-patch` attributes the default proxyHandler fallback to the same commit. `git log --all --full-history -S'x-base-url' -- app/api/proxy.ts` finds the creation commit plus only the later DALL-E-related edit 2b0f2e5f9d064bc8107414b0c2e7efe61c03cdef; `git log --all --full-history -S'return proxyHandler'` finds only f652f7326070dfbffcc5f90a999e95df21f4c650. Thus this commit first wrote both necessary parts of the reported mechanism and is not a later move/refactor/backport.

Immediate-parent verification: `git ls-tree -r b2965e1deb48f9e63aabecb1d477185d22f19e1f -- app/api/proxy.ts app/api/[provider]/[...path]/route.ts` returns only route.ts (blob 06e3e51603c3e162303ca25836a2371ea25cc77d), proving app/api/proxy.ts is absent. `git show b2965e...:app/api/[provider]/[...path]/route.ts` shows no proxyHandler import and sends the default case to openaiHandler. Therefore the attacker-controlled generic proxy path is absent in the direct parent tree.

Version boundary: `git tag --contains f652f7326070dfbffcc5f90a999e95df21f4c650 --sort=version:refname` starts at v2.15.0 and includes every release through the last tag v2.16.1. v2.14.2 (495b321d0afa9e23a256fde18f1d2ec60c54e34b, dated 2024-08-16) has only the pre-BIC provider route and no app/api/proxy.ts, while v2.15.0 (fe5a4f4447a14c8864bbad26ec10651a338886c2, dated 2024-09-07) contains route blob 24aa5ec040f1700fa72d138b1e893e198588efc6 and proxy blob 731003aa1ea1a08aeeab76d8348d954bc6b84751. For this exact mechanism, v2.15.0 is the first tagged vulnerable release; v2.16.1 remains vulnerable, matching the advisory's upper affected boundary.

Unpatched status/fix search: the complete `git log --all --follow -- app/api/proxy.ts` contains only f652f7326070dfbffcc5f90a999e95df21f4c650, 2b0f2e5f9d064bc8107414b0c2e7efe61c03cdef, and 18a657188339ac96905f0eaadd0583fdd6001f65. The latter two merely add server-side OpenAI-key handling and retain the unrestricted destination fetch. Tag v2.16.1 and default-branch HEAD defdcdb55d850cd12c4c657eb83729fd66e215c0 resolve app/api/proxy.ts to the identical vulnerable blob b3e5e7b7b9309be2357a4c2b529495207740fbe1 and the provider route to e8af34f29f895b86f8378a93d465131b6e3fccc3. HEAD is dated 2026-08-11, after the 2026-04 report, and still has the x-base-url fetch plus unknown-provider fallback. No upstream fix or patched tag exists in the validated clone, so fix_sha and direct_fix_sha are null.

BIC-only AI check: `git cat-file commit f652f7326070dfbffcc5f90a999e95df21f4c650` yields tree 206cf249917ff619323a2d9ca58e96cd34030404, parent b2965e1deb48f9e63aabecb1d477185d22f19e1f, author and committer `lloydzhou <lloydzhou@qq.com> 1725271879 +0800`, and only the message `plugin add auth config`; there are no trailers and no bot identity. Hosted commit metadata likewise identifies @lloydzhou and the same single parent. No PR-body, branch-name, later-commit, or fix-only signal was used for attribution.
reasoning: The report's exploit requires two causal elements: a public dispatch path that selects the generic proxy and a proxy that treats request-controlled destination data as trusted. Line history and the creation diff converge on f652f7326070dfbffcc5f90a999e95df21f4c650, which added both elements together. Direct inspection of its parent proves the proxy file did not exist and unknown providers still used the constrained OpenAI handler, so this is the smallest real BIC rather than a move or later edit. The release trees place that BIC after v2.14.2 and in v2.15.0 through v2.16.1. Later proxy commits do not add destination validation, and the latest default-branch tree retains the exact vulnerable blobs; consequently the vulnerability remains unpatched and there is no honest fix SHA or patched-version boundary to report. Finally, attribution is restricted to the BIC commit object: it contains only a normal human author/committer and no AI/co-author/generated/bot marker. The closed causal verdict is therefore NOT_AI despite the missing upstream fix.
remaining_gap: Upstream remains unpatched in default-branch HEAD defdcdb55d850cd12c4c657eb83729fd66e215c0 as of 2026-08-11, and the public report/advisory names no patched release. Consequently no fix_sha, direct_fix_sha, or patched version boundary exists yet; this is an unpatched-status gap, not uncertainty about the BIC or AI verdict.
